verdict.rationale: Users report that Name.com supports two-factor and multi-factor authentication. The docs show API tokens issued under Account Settings → Security, with separate development and production tokens, used via HTTP Basic Auth. Nothing shows the tokens can be limited by permission or resource, and nothing mentions IP allowlisting for API access. Missing for 10: first-party 2FA documentation, scoped or least-privilege API credentials, IP allowlisting on API access.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the registrar account itself is defensible — real 2FA, scoped API credentials, and IP allowlisting on API access

citations.quote: One of the reasons we liked name.com was their multi-factor support and email on action support
Go to Account Settings → Security → API Tokens and issue both development and production tokens
The Core API uses **HTTP Basic Authentication** with your name.com API credentials.
